_comment: Curated industry/actor -> high-relevance ATT&CK technique profiles for
threat-informed gap weighting (MITRE Phase 11). DETERMINISTIC input to
ranking.build_threat_profile — never touches coverage %, only lifts
profile-relevant gaps above equal-tier peers in the ranked gap list.
Every technique ID must resolve 'ok' against the pinned attack.json
(enforced by test_mitre_threat_profile.py). Industry keys are the
LOWERCASE of the /mitre/new wizard's INDUSTRIES values; aliases fold
related wizard options onto one profile. Actor keys are display names
offered by GET /api/v1/mitre/threat-catalog.
Sources: MITRE ATT&CK Groups pages (G-codes cited per actor), Verizon
DBIR 2025 industry snapshots, CISA #StopRansomware advisories (incl.
AA23-325A LockBit, AA23-320A Scattered Spider, AA24-038A Volt Typhoon),
Mandiant M-Trends 2025, HHS HC3 healthcare sector reports, FS-ISAC
annual report, Dragos OT/ICS Year in Review 2025.
Curation rule: 8-12 techniques per entry, only behaviors repeatedly
attributed in public reporting — high-confidence over exhaustive.
Plan phase A8 (2026-08-03) added 9 industries (Professional Services,
Media & Entertainment, Hospitality & Food Service, Pharmaceuticals &
Life Sciences, Agriculture & Food Production, Mining & Metals,
Aerospace & Defense, Construction & Engineering, Maritime & Shipping),
10 actors (APT1, APT10, Kimsuky, APT33, APT34/OilRig, FIN8, Carbanak
Group, Turla, Mustang Panda, Indrik Spider), and region_profiles (NA/
Europe/APAC/MEA/LATAM, coarse keyword-matched free text -> curated
actor lists), same curation discipline and sourcing standard as the
Phase 11 seed set; every new technique id verified against the pinned
v19.1 dataset before being added.

FIN7.note: Financially motivated; phishing-to-backdoor intrusions, later ransomware affiliations.

Lazarus Group.note: DPRK-attributed; financial theft + espionage, trojanized installers.

APT28.note: GRU-attributed; credential harvesting, password spraying, phishing.

APT41.note: Dual espionage + financially motivated; web-facing app exploitation, web shells.

Sandworm Team.note: GRU-attributed; destructive operations against energy/critical infrastructure.

Volt Typhoon.note: PRC-attributed; living-off-the-land pre-positioning in critical infrastructure (CISA AA24-038A).

Scattered Spider.note: Help-desk social engineering, MFA fatigue, RMM abuse, data-theft extortion (CISA AA23-320A).

LockBit affiliates.note: RaaS affiliates per CISA AA23-325A; commodity intrusion to encryption/exfiltration.

APT1.note: PLA Unit 61398 / Comment Crew; large-scale IP theft espionage (Mandiant's 2013 APT1 report).

APT10.note: PRC-attributed; Cloud Hopper MSP/supply-chain compromise for IP theft.

Kimsuky.note: DPRK-attributed; espionage against government/think-tank/nuclear-research targets via phishing.

APT33.note: Iran-attributed; energy-sector espionage, spearphishing, destructive-capable tooling.

APT34.note: OilRig; Iran-attributed Middle East government/energy espionage, notable for DNS-tunneled C2.

FIN8.note: Financially motivated; POS-malware campaigns against hospitality/retail.

Carbanak Group.note: Financially motivated; banking + POS malware against finance/hospitality, later ransomware overlap with FIN7.

Turla.note: Russia-attributed; long-running government/diplomatic espionage, watering holes, satellite-based C2.

Mustang Panda.note: PRC-attributed; NGO/government espionage via malicious archives and removable-media propagation.

Indrik Spider.note: Evil Corp; Dridex/BitPaymer/WastedLocker operators, big-game ransomware against finance.
